newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends unchanged as c. bank sells.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends unchanged as c. bank sells.

text.p: The limited intervention of Philippine central bank aided the peso to close unchanged at 29 pesos to the dollar, traders said on Tuesday.
However, banks remained uneasy as the central bank's dollar sale was not enough to meet the huge demand. The central bank was selling $500,000 each to selected banks.
The peso opened at 30 pesos, a 13.6 percent drop since the central bank loosened its grip on the currency last Friday.
It steadily gained ground after the central bank intervened, accounting for almost half of the day's volume of $46 million, by selling between 29.70 and 29 pesos, traders said.
"The market is still bullish on the dollar. A lot of banks are short of dollars. That's why banks are wary of selling dollars," a dealer said.
"(But) there is still the possibility the central bank may raise its rate up to a point where it hurts," he added.
Late last week, the central bank raised its overnight borrowing rate to a 2-1/2 year high of 32 percent to fight off speculation.
